hook: Zebrafish lack MLKL and so have no canonical necroptosis, yet their RIPK3 still works
summary: Necroptosis is a form of programmed cell death that normally needs the protein MLKL. The team confirmed zebrafish lack it, and showed that fish missing Caspase-8 live to adulthood, unlike mice, where that loss is lethal. Overexpressing Ripk3 did not kill Caspase-8-deficient embryos. The evidence is genetic and from one species, so it says little about how other fish handle cell death.
title: Zebrafish lack canonical necroptosis despite retaining functional RIPK3
